approved: Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Take Home Pay of All Workers) Bill 2017

The speaker moved the Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Take Home Pay of All Workers) Bill 2017, arguing the Fair Work Commission’s penalty rate cuts were wrong and that some workers had already lost penalty rates through union-negotiated deals. Specific examples cited include Vinpac in the Hunter Valley reducing Sunday pay from $207.12 to $107.46, Cleanevent Australia cutting Sunday rates from double time to zero, and KFC in Queensland and Tweed Heads eliminating Sunday penalty rates for 4,229 workers at a cost of $60.65 per Sunday shift.

The speaker argued in support of the Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Take Home Pay of All Workers) Bill 2017, which negates Sunday penalty rate reductions for retail, fast food, hospitality, and tourism industries and allows workers to revert to award penalty rates if worse off under a new enterprise agreement. The speaker urged Labor to allow debate on the bill in the chamber.

The speaker presented minutes from the Standing Committee on Employment, Education and Training's inquiry into the Fair Work Amendment (Protecting Take Home Pay of All Workers) Bill 2017, following a prior statement about discharging the committee's reporting obligation.
